newsitem.title: UK: Tarmac outlook for 1997 and beyond improved.
newsitem.headline: Tarmac outlook for 1997 and beyond improved.

text.p: Building group Tarmac Plc described its outlook for 1997 and beyond as "much improved" on Tuesday and added that British markets had kicked off well this year.

Tarmac reported year pretax profits of 75.5 million pounds. It froze the dividend at 5.5 pence per share, as expected by many, and the 1996 profits were above market forecasts before exceptional items. After restructuring charges of 65 million pounds were included, profits fell to 10.5 million for the year.

The internal shake-up, resulting in the one-off charge, stemmed from Tarmac's integration of the former George Wimpey Plc minerals and construction businesses which were acquired in an asset swap for Tarmac's housing business.

Tarmac chief executive Neville Simms said in the results statement "Using our current portfolio of activities as a platform, we will continue to focus on improved earnings and cash flow...Across the group we are beginning to enjoy the benefits of additional growth opportunities and (the) stronger foundation creation in 1996 at home and overseas."

Highlights of the 1996 results showed total operating profit up 29 percent before exceptionals, and the benefits of the rationalisation reaching 38 million pounds ($61.8 million) - double the original estimate.

Heavy building materials saw operating profit up 27 percent and progress in North America. Construction saw its contracting margins rise to 1.4 percent from 0.9 percent in 1995. ($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
